claims.text: Russian forces launched a heavy missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight into Thursday.
Kyiv officials reported at least 16 people were killed in and around the city during the aerial attack.
Authorities reported that 33 people were injured in Kyiv during the overnight bombardment.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko stated that homes, a school, and a children's medical center were damaged in the attack.
Ukraine's air force reported that Russia launched 168 drones alongside dozens of ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic missiles.
Ukraine's air force reported shooting down 41 out of 46 cruise missiles and 145 drones launched by Russia.
Ukraine's air force stated that none of the high-speed ballistic missiles launched by Russia were intercepted.
Eight people were reported killed in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district during the attack.
Tymur Tkachenko, governor of the Kyiv region, said a strike in Brovary district killed one man and wounded another.
Romania's defence ministry stated a drone entered Romanian airspace near Galați and crashed in Tulcea county.
The State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that at least 17 people were killed across Kyiv in the overnight strikes.
The State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that more than 40 people were injured across Kyiv.
Ukraine relies on American supplies of Patriot interceptor missiles to defend against Russian ballistic missiles.
Russia's defence ministry claimed that 726 Ukrainian drones were shot down over various regions in Russia.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the US intends to collapse the Iranian regime through economic measures.
US President Donald Trump warned that any country providing a lifeline to Iran will face tremendous economic consequences.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed that further details of the US economic plan against Iran will be announced on August 24.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February.
The US and Iran agreed to ceasefires in April and June to facilitate negotiations to end the conflict.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that the US would apply the toughest sanctions in history on Iran.
The US administration designated 10 people associated with Hezbollah, including a Turkish businessman, expanding sanctions against Iran's allies.
Iran's foreign ministry characterized US economic sanctions as 'economic terrorism' and 'crimes against humanity'.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that US economic threats aim to divert US public attention from domestic financial problems.
Iranian consul general in Mumbai Saeid Reza Mosayeb Motlagh rejected Donald Trump's claim that the US has total control over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US fulfills commitments under a Memorandum of Understanding.
The United Arab Emirates suspended all trade activities and financial transactions with Iran after detecting two missiles launched from the country.
Prior to the war, the United Arab Emirates provided more than 30% of Iran's imports.
The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court sentenced Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison and confiscated all of his personal property.
Hui Ka Yan pleaded guilty in April to eight charges including misuse of funds, fundraising fraud, and bribery.
The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court fined Evergrande Group 8.8 billion yuan and its property arm 7 billion yuan.
Evergrande defaulted on most of its $300 billion in liabilities after the Chinese government introduced regulations limiting developer debt in 2020.
More than 50 individuals linked to Evergrande were sentenced on Thursday, receiving prison terms ranging from 20 months to 18 years.
Hong Kong and mainland Chinese authorities found Evergrande overstated revenues by roughly $80 billion over 2019 and 2020.
Hui Ka Yan's sons, Xu Zhijian and Xu Tenghe, were among the Evergrande executives sentenced to jail terms ranging from 22 months to 18 years.
In March 2024, Hui Ka Yan was fined $6.5 million and banned for life from China's capital market.
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected President of Bangladesh after defeating challenger Oli Ahmed by 255 votes to 88.
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir served as secretary-general of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party.
Former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned halfway through his term last month.
In the Bangladeshi presidential election, 343 out of 349 registered voting lawmakers participated.
This presidential election was the first contested presidential vote in Bangladesh since 1991.
Alamgir will take office as Bangladesh's 23rd President.
Parliamentary Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad served as acting president following Shahabuddin's resignation.
Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was sentenced to be hanged after being found guilty in absentia of crimes against humanity.
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad under heavy security.
A three-judge panel of Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered that Imran Khan be taken to a hospital within 48 hours for medical examination.
Imran Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on corruption charges.
In February, Imran Khan's lawyer stated he had only 15% vision left in his right eye.
Imran Khan's next court hearing is scheduled for September 16, and his lawyer stated he should remain hospitalized until at least then.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry affirmed the Pakistani government would fully comply with the Supreme Court ruling regarding Imran Khan.
Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry stated the government could consider medical treatment abroad for Imran Khan if adequate care was unavailable domestically.
North Korea launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters on Thursday.
South Korea's military reported the missiles were launched from the Pyongyang area at around 5pm (08.00 GMT).
The US and South Korea scaled back their 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises following orders from Donald Trump.
Donald Trump cited his relationship with Kim Jong-un and South Korea's refusal to support the US war against Iran as reasons for scaling back military drills.
Kim Yo-jong dismissed Trump's reduction of joint military exercises, stating the aggressive nature of the drills remained unchanged.
Kim Yo-jong denied Donald Trump's assertion that Kim Jong-un had responded to a request for a conversation.
Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would be meeting Kim Jong-un later this year.
The Israeli military admitted its troops opened fire in 2024 on a car in Gaza carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six family members.
The Israeli military announced a criminal investigation by its military police into the killing of Hind Rajab and her family.
The Israeli military admitted its troops fired on a Red Crescent ambulance dispatched to rescue Hind Rajab, killing two medics.
The Israeli military initiated a criminal investigation into the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinian medics and humanitarian personnel near Rafah.
Israeli troops bulldozed the bodies and emergency vehicles of the 15 killed personnel into a mass grave near Rafah.
The Israeli military decided against opening a criminal investigation into the April 2024 airstrikes that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers.
Research agencies Forensics Architecture and Earshot mapped 335 bullet holes on the car carrying Hind Rajab.
The Health Ministry in Gaza reported that more than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza during Israel's military campaign.
A petition was filed in the Supreme Court of India seeking a CBI investigation into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.
Three members of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission have resigned following examination irregularity allegations.
The Jharkhand High Court stayed state government notifications cancelling appointments made through the 11th and 13th JPSC examinations.
Justice Deepak Roshan of the Jharkhand High Court directed the state government to file its reply by September 15.
The High Court order permits affected employees selected through the 11th and 13th JPSC exams to continue holding their positions while petitions are heard.
Protesting student leaders announced plans to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren across all 24 districts of Jharkhand.
On August 18, the Jharkhand government cancelled 22 examinations and ordered a probe into 23 others conducted since 2014.
A nine-judge Supreme Court bench held that the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply judgment's definition of 'industry' will not apply to Section 2(p) of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
The Supreme Court ruled that pending labor disputes under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, will continue to be decided based on the 1978 judgment.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant authored the majority opinion for the nine-judge bench.
Justice B.V. Nagarathna, joined by Justices Dipankar Datta and Ujjal Bhuyan, dissented, holding that reconsidering the 1978 judgment was unwarranted.
The 1978 triple test for defining an industry requires systematic activity, functional cooperation between employer and employees, and production of goods or services.
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020, came into force on November 21, 2025.
The Indian government allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh (1 million) tonnes of raw sugar for the first time in a decade.
The food ministry capped sugar inventories for bulk consumers using over 10 tonnes a month to a maximum of 15 days of consumption.
The stockholding restrictions for bulk sugar consumers will apply from September 1 to November 30.
Average retail sugar prices in India reached Rs 52.3 per kg, representing a 13% increase from a year earlier.
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade set October 31, 2026, as the deadline for duty-free raw sugar imports under the Tariff Rate Quota.
The all-India average ex-mill sugar price rose to Rs 5,400-5,500 per quintal, up from Rs 3,900 a year earlier.
The Supreme Court formed a five-member high-powered enquiry committee led by retired judge R Subhash Reddy to probe police actions during a July 20 student protest march to Parliament.
The enquiry committee members include former CJ Ravi S Jha, former judge Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla, and former DGP LR Bishnoi.
Delhi Police reported in an affidavit that 248 police personnel and 218 protesters were injured during the July 20 demonstrations.
The student protests were organized by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) against alleged paper leaks in national examinations.
Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down from his position as Union Education Minister on July 25 following paper leak protests.
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital after demonstrating in solidarity with CJP.
